hero.title: File:Warhol silver trunk 03.jpg
hero.description: Oblique view of a silver painted trunk, owned by Andy Warhol, on display at the Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. This trunk was used in Warhol's Silver Factory as a storage unit and film prop. Edie Sedgwick sits on this trunk in Warhol's film Vinyl. After Warhol's death in 1987 inside the trunk were found photographs, and photographic negatives by Billy Name, as well at the script of "Up Your Ass" by Valerie Solanas, which Warhol repeatedly told Solanas he had lost. This was one of the compounding reasons Solanas shot Warhol in 1968.

gallery.title: File:860 Broadway.jpg
gallery.description: 860 Broadway, on the corner of East 17th Street on the north boundary of Union Square in Manhattan, New York City was built in 1883-84 and was designed by Detlef Lienau in the late 19th-century commercial style.  It extends through the block to 18th Street (#32-34). Originally called the Parish Building, it was later the Butler Building, and is located within the Ladies' Mile Historic District. (Source:  "NYCLPC Ladies' Mile Historic District Designation Report, volume 2") 860 Broadway was the third location of Andy Warhol's "Factory".

gallery.description: The photograph shows the original site on East 47th Street in Midtown Manhattan. To the right of the red-brick residential building stood the first Factory of Andy Warhol, known as the “Silver Factory,” from 1963 to 1967. The original building was later demolished and replaced by a parking structure.

gallery.title: File:The Factory – dnešní podoba místa u YMCA na East 47th Street, NYC.jpg
gallery.description: The photograph shows the present-day site of Andy Warhol’s first Factory, known as the “Silver Factory,” which operated from 1963 to 1967. It was located to the right of the red-brick residential building at 231 East 47th Street in Midtown Manhattan. The original structure was later demolished and replaced by a parking facility. The adjacent Vanderbilt YMCA building helps identify the location.
